shots.phrase: Begin by framing Pipeline Foundation: Vertex Processing as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Consider this worked case: Vertex attributes like position and normal are passed from the application to the vertex shader for initial transformation.
This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.
Now define Primitive Assembly precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: Three consecutive vertex indices are connected to form a triangle primitive that defines a planar surface.
A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
With the foundation in place, examine how View Volume Clipping operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: A triangle extending beyond the camera's frustum is clipped at the clipping plane boundaries.
The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
Next, compare the choices involved in Rasterization Conversion and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: Each triangle is subdivided into a set of pixels, generating a fragment for every covered pixel.
Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
Apply Interpolation Values to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: Color and normal values are linearly interpolated across the triangle to determine per-fragment properties.
The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
Examine the tradeoffs in Fragment Processing, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Consider this worked case: The fragment shader calculates final color, alpha, and depth values for each pixel.
Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
Stress-test the reasoning around Depth Testing Visibility with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Depth testing resolves visibility according to stored depth values.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Blending Operations to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Blending combines a fragment result with an existing framebuffer value.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Coordinate Spaces and Sampling to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: Texture coordinates are explicitly mapped from object space to UV space to avoid sampling artifacts.
The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Consider this worked case: A checklist verifies explicit coordinate mappings, proper sampling rates, and error bounds before rendering.
The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
